html:
The Southern Sierra Miwok are a Miwok people of the western Sierra Nevada in California, along the upper Merced and Chowchilla rivers. Their land included Yosemite Valley, whose people were called the Ahwahneechee.

They gathered acorns, the staple food, and pounded them in holes worn into granite, and they hunted deer and fished. Many married with the Mono Paiute across the mountains.

The Gold Rush brought miners onto their land from 1849. In 1851 the Mariposa Battalion, a state militia, entered Yosemite Valley chasing the people of chief Tenaya, the first outsiders to see it. Their neighbours include the Central Sierra Miwok and the Yokuts.
